prompt: A resident aHerald process that is still running from an older build closes the pipe (error 800700e9) when a newer hook sends it an event that carries a field the older build does not know. Make decoding of an event ignore unknown event fields so an older resident keeps accepting events. The request wrapper itself must stay strict about unknown fields. Add a regression test and run focused checks.

In resident mode the card queue ticks every 15 s while idle (usage polling). A card that arrives after such an idle tick expires too early: the first tick after it arrives charges the whole idle gap against the card's display time. A card's display time should only count time while the card is shown, starting from the first tick that selects it. Fix this, add a regression test, and run focused checks.

In a live Claude Code session a PermissionRequest event and a permission_prompt Notification for the same session arrived 6 s apart, beyond deduplicate_ms (1500 ms), and two cards were shown. A Claude wait (permission) card that is still open should absorb repeated permission prompts from the same session regardless of the time gap. Another session still gets its own card, and once the session reports that its turn completed, a new permission request creates a new card. Fix this, add a regression test, and run focused checks.

Clicking a card for a Claude terminal (CLI) session delays the first click by several seconds on a cold disk cache: the Desktop session lookup reads every session file before the recorded terminal window is focused, although it can never match a terminal session. Focus the recorded window first and fall back to the Desktop lookup only when no window is recorded or focusing it fails. Fix this, update or add tests, and run focused checks.

The usage summary labels the weekly window 'week' and shows long countdowns in whole days only. Label the weekly window '7d' and show countdowns of a day or more as '<days>d <hours>h' with hours rounded down: 86400 s is '1d 0h', 89999 s is '1d 0h', 90000 s is '1d 1h', 172799 s is '1d 23h', 172800 s is '2d 0h', 558000 s is '6d 11h'. Countdowns under a day keep their current format. Example line: 'Codex remain: 5h 25% / 2:35, 7d 10% / 6d 11h'. Update tests and run focused checks.

The tray menu and tooltip usage line does not say whether the figures are remaining or used. Put the configured usage display mode in the label: 'Codex remain: 5h 25% / 2:35, week 10% / 6d' or 'Codex used: 5h 75% / 2:35, week 90% / 6d'. The status-only form 'Codex: <status>' gets the same label, 'Codex <mode>: <status>'. Update tests and run focused checks.
